passages.text:
[Accuracy of PHQ-2/PHQ-9 and GAD-2/GAD-7 screening questionnaires > Screening questionnaires used by MapleMind > Depression: PHQ-2 then PHQ-9]
- PHQ-2 scores range 0-6; PHQ-9 scores range 0-27. - An individual participant data meta-analysis (44 studies, 10,627 participants) found that PHQ-2 score of 2 or more followed by PHQ-9 score of 10 or more had sensitivity 0.82, specificity 0.87 and AUC 0.90, not significantly different in sensitivity from PHQ-9 alone (0.86). - This two-stage approach lets most people answer only 2 questions, which is why MapleMind uses it to cap follow-up questions. - PHQ-9 severity bands: 0-4 minimal, 5-9 mild, 10-14 moderate, 15-19 moderately severe, 20-27 severe. - PHQ-9 item 9 asks about thoughts of being better off dead or self-harm; any non-zero answer requires immediate safety follow-up regardless of total score.

passages.text:
[CANMAT 2023 update on clinical guidelines for major depressive disorder in adults (summary) > CANMAT 2023 depression guideline - summary for navigation]
- CANMAT published its previous depression guideline in 2016; the 2023 update was developed by an editorial group of academic clinicians and patient partners, based on systematic reviews and meta-analyses published since 2015. - Recommendations are organized by lines of treatment, informed by levels of evidence plus clinical support (expert consensus on safety, tolerability and feasibility). - The update emphasizes a collaborative, personalized and systematic (measurement-based) approach to managing depression. - Treatment options discussed include psychological treatments, pharmacotherapy, lifestyle interventions and neuromodulation; choice depends on severity, patient preference and clinical assessment. - More than one in ten Canadians will experience depression at some point in their lives, and it is estimated that only about 20% receive adequate treatment (UBC news release, 2024).

answer:
**Your check-in summary** (screening, not a diagnosis)
- Mood (PHQ): score 12 - moderate range - worth discussing with a health professional
- Anxiety (GAD): brief screen score 5 - above the threshold; completing the full questionnaire with a clinician is recommended
- Stopped after 12 questions (question budget); remaining items can be completed with a clinician.

Measurement-based care supports using validated questionnaires such as the PHQ-9 to track symptoms over time and share them with a clinician [1]. Many Canadians who screen positive for depression or anxiety, or who want help with weight-related health, have no regular clinician to follow up with [2]. The update emphasizes a collaborative, personalized and systematic (measurement-based) approach to managing depression [4].

**Sources**
[1] CANMAT 2023 update on clinical guidelines for major depressive disorder in adults (summary) - Canadian Network for Mood and Anxiety Treatments, Canadian Journal of Psychiatry 69(9):641-687 (2024-05-08). https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11351064/
[2] OurCare National Survey 2025 - access to primary care in Canada - MAP Centre for Urban Health Solutions, Unity Health Toronto, with the Canadian Medical Association (2025-12-08). https://unityhealth.to/2025/12/access-to-primary-care-growing/
[4] CANMAT 2023 update on clinical guidelines for major depressive disorder in adults (summary) - Canadian Network for Mood and Anxiety Treatments, Canadian Journal of Psychiatry 69(9):641-687 (2024-05-08). https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11351064/

**Where to get support**
- 9-8-8 Suicide Crisis Helpline: Call or text 9-8-8 (24/7)
- Emergency services: 9-1-1 (24/7)
- Kids Help Phone: 1-800-668-6868 or text CONNECT to 686868 (24/7)
- Hope for Wellness Help Line: 1-855-242-3310 (24/7)
- National Eating Disorder Information Centre (NEDIC): 1-866-633-4220 (see nedic.ca)
- Most provinces: dial 8-1-1 to talk to a registered nurse (tell me your province for the exact service).
- Community counselling: find your local Canadian Mental Health Association branch - https://cmha.ca/find-your-cmha/
- No family doctor? Walk-in clinics, pharmacists and 8-1-1 can help you start; ask about publicly funded counselling.

_MapleMind gives general information, not medical advice or diagnosis. In an emergency call 9-1-1; in crisis call or text 9-8-8._
